phase_5_stateless_menu.notes: Session 2 (2026-08-30) — PLAN TABLE (written before code, per contract). Baseline verified on fresh clone: npm ci then npm test = 145/145 (phase-4 checkpoint accurate; the 6 initial failures were only missing node_modules). STATE SURFACE AUDIT — everything getState/putState/clearFlow currently carries: (A) state.flow + state.pending: the 12 input flows below. (B) state.activeViewId: the single self-editing view id (views.js renderInteractiveView/renderFreshView + the bug-01 reset in handleMessage). (C) state.currentTask: write-only leftover (set in startJob/startRelayJob after ensureTaskLabel, NEVER read anywhere) — dead, deleted outright. ENCODING DECISIONS: - Menu edits become message_id-implicit: every button-driven render edits callback.message.message_id; every user-message-driven render sends fresh (bug-01 behavior kept). activeViewId persistence deleted; views.js renderInteractiveView(messageId=null => fresh send, no getState/putState). - freeTextReply(env, chatId, text, options?) in telegram.js: sendMessage with reply_markup {force_reply:true, selective:true} (plus inline keyboard only when a Cancel/choice row is needed — Telegram allows both markups together; the inline rows go on the SAME message object). Returns the sent Message. - parseFlowReply(message) in new pure module src/flow.js: reads message.reply_to_message; returns {opcode,args,messageId} iff reply_to_message.from.is_bot && text parses marker '[cf] cf:[:arg…]' (single-line marker comment at the bottom of every prompt; documented in ARCHITECTURE.md). Matching is by OPCODE STRING, not message_id (message_id is only reported for callers that need to edit the prompt, e.g. clone progress) — matches the contract ('keyed off message.reply_to_message'). - Pending flow context is re-derived per reply: credentials come from KV getCredentials (allowed); jobId for upload_plan re-resolved via getJobIdForLabel(pending label arg). NO chat-state record is ever written for navigation. FLOW-BY-FLOW MAPPING (12 flows): 1. wizard (multi-step: source/focus text + duration/music buttons + confirm): - Text steps (source incl. .torrent/video documents, focus): prompt carries invisible marker 'cf:wzsrc' / 'cf:wzfoc' + force_reply; wizard record encoded in marker args. - Wizard state travels as opaque token arg on every wz:* callback_data and as marker args: legacy base64url(JSON wizard) prefixed '1' (v1). ~92 bytes for a fresh wizard => under the 64-byte CALLBACK cap it only rides as marker text (no cap on message text); for callbacks the token is NOT round-tripped — instead every wizard BUTTON message is itself a marker-bearing prompt? NO — simpler split: button-only steps (length/music/confirm) encode wizard fields FLATTENED in callback_data: 'wz:dur::' would exceed 64B. DECISION: button steps carry the full wizard inline: jobId(manual-<13digits>) + step + series(1bit) + duration + music-code fit; source/focus text DO NOT fit => source/focus completion is communicated via the user's force_reply REPLY whose reply_to_message chain anchors the wizard, and subsequent button steps re-encode from (a) flattened fields in the current message's marker + (b) the just-answered text. The full wizard object therefore lives ONLY in the latest prompt message's marker comment as base64url JSON (message text, no size cap); every wizard render embeds 'cf:wzs:' (step prompts) and button callbacks read it back from callback.message.text via parseWizardMarker(). callback_data stays tiny ('wz:dur:60' etc., unchanged). This is exactly 'encode the current step directly into each inline keyboard's message' — the keyboard's message carries the state. - wz:cancel / wz:back mutate the marker-carried wizard and re-render (edit). Expiry case = message has no parseable marker (e.g. very old message) => 'wizard expired, /new' (same UX as today). 2. upload_plan (label arg): prompt marker 'cf:upl:

phase_6_remove_botA_dedup.notes:
Session 4 (2026-08-30): Bot A's own update dedup removed; webhook is idempotent by construction. REMOVED: markUpdateSeen + UPDATE_TTL_SECONDS + the telegram:update:{id} KV key from storage.js; the import and the `if (await markUpdateSeen(env, update.update_id)) return;` gate from index.js handleUpdate; the stale comment at the waitUntil call site rewritten to state the no-dedup invariant. storage.js header now documents: KV = credentials + relay staging only.

IDEMPOTENCY AUDIT — every handler reachable from handleUpdate, and why a Telegram redelivery of the same update is safe:
1) Navigation/menu callbacks (menu:*/set:*/task list views, views.js renders): pure render operations — editMessage of an existing view or a fresh send; re-execution reproduces the same visible state, no stored record created.
2) Force_reply/flow handlers (phase 5 handleFlowReply: wzs/upl/uplb/clname/patnew/patc/repo/gemkey/wm/news/zkey/zsch/tpm/tppm/mupl): credentials writes are idempotent KV puts of the same value (encrypted envelope of the same PAT); plan-upload buffer accumulation is carried in chat-visible markers and re-derives the same buffer from the same reply chain; a duplicate reply reprocesses the same fragment set.
3) startJob (wizard confirm, L622): dispatches Stage A with a FIXED job_id from the wizard token (manual-<ts>) — a redelivered confirm re-dispatches the SAME workflow name + SAME job_id + SAME code_ref. GitHub treats repeated workflow_dispatch of the same workflow as a new run, so the pre-dispatch task guard applies: ensureTaskLabel reuses the existing label/job for that chat, and the job's own pipeline writes are upsert-style (putBinaryFile with identical path+content+message produces an identical commit shape; re-upload of the same bytes is content-addressed). RESIDUAL RISK (documented): a redelivery arriving while the first run is still queued can create a second Stage A run for the same job_id — both runs write the same job folder with the same content, so the end state converges; worst case is one redundant Actions run, never corrupt state.
4) startRelayJob (L748): stages via putRelayJob (idempotent KV put of the same staged record keyed on the same ids) then startJob — same convergence argument as (3); Bot B's OWN relay dedup (alreadySeenRelayUpdate/markRelayUpdateSeen) still guards the relay group path and is untouched.
5) dispatchZernioPublish / dispatchZernioPostAction (L884/917, incl. force_reply manual-schedule paths L971/983): dispatch the publish workflow with action+label/postId resolved from the same marker args; the tppm handler re-validates POST_ID_PATTERN before dispatch. A redelivered button press re-dispatches the same action — Zernio-side operations are publish/cancel/update of a specific post id; repeating 'cancel' or 'update' of the same post is a safe re-application, and 'publish_now' of an already-published post is rejected/no-ops at the Zernio layer. RESIDUAL RISK (documented): same class as (3) — a duplicate queued Actions run at worst.
6) Stage A/B re-dispatch sites (L1349/1389/1408/1528/1663): all re-dispatch an EXISTING job_id derived from stored task state (retry/resume semantics) — these are already the 'run again for this job' paths, so a duplicate delivery is indistinguishable from the intended retry UX.
7) putBinaryFile call sites (torrent staging L615, audio-library L2679): same path + same bytes + same commit message => convergent content; a duplicate upload of the identical file produces the identical tree.
8) Shadow Clone cron sweep (runCloneJobSweep/tickCloneJob): cron-driven, not webhook-driven; getCloneJob/putCloneJob are D1 upserts by chat_id and pollShadowCloneJob is a read — re-ticks are the designed operating mode (bug-51).
9) announce/news/deploy-failure senders: gated by the announcements D1 markers (one row per chat+kind, upsert) — a duplicate update cannot re-announce the same marker.

Bot B relay dedup (alreadySeenRelayUpdate/markRelayUpdateSeen in relay-worker.js, RELAY_UPDATE_TTL_SECONDS) explicitly NOT touched.

Single-message pastes and .json files are unchanged (reply to the upload prompt).

phase_5 documented assumption: the Gemini key entry UI (set:gemini:add) has been unreachable since bug-30 removed Automatic mode; the flow was converted to force_reply anyway (zero-cost) rather than deleted, to keep this migration storage-only.

phase_5 step 5.3 documented assumption: the ⏳ receiving-indicator, originally a plain sendMessage in the legacy code, is now a sendForceReply so subsequent fragment bubbles arrive as reply_to_message. editMessageText cannot change reply_markup type, but the force_reply behavior of the ORIGINAL Telegram message is preserved across text edits — the next reply still routes back to the indicator via handleFlowReply's 'uplb' case. If Telegram behavior ever changes here, the fallback (deleted-indicator branch re-sends via sendForceReply) still recovers state from the buffer marker on the new indicator.
